question: Do maintained shared definitions keep agents correct after data changes, and at what cost, compared with published agent memories?
authorization: User 2026-10-31: redo the Fig. 6 experiment on the DeepSeek official API, about CNY 40.
bank: select-bank.py on the model-free probe: single-month (P1) and period-difference (T1) questions of every metric that reads a written table, per phase; bank-synthetic.json and bank-tpch.json are frozen before the first paid call and identical for all methods and runs.
agents: One agent A learns (six learning questions, two per metric, with the business definition and a verified answer) and answers every scored question by metric name only. Every question starts a new conversation.
memory_scope: ACE and AWM keep agent A's memory; G-Memory shares within the database; MAVRA keeps global definitions. Each change starts from v1 data and the post-held-out memory of the method.
feedback: All four methods receive the same bounded record of their own three latest questions, answers, SQL, observations and binary correctness. No reference answer, reference SQL or change label reaches any method.
shared_prompt: All methods use the same planner prompt, including the business-key rule; MAVRA additionally has its native metric tools and their usage rule.
scoring: An answer is correct when it equals the reference answer at the question's precision. Clarification requests and errors count as not correct and are reported separately (correct / clarification / wrong).
aggregation: Primary: answers pooled per group (micro accuracy), per schema and over both schemas, mean over runs with the range over runs. Per-change and per-run tables are kept in full. Tokens per question include online memory updates and MAVRA's learning-time extraction and optimization charged to the run.
pilot: Run 1 is the pilot. If a defect is found in any method's harness, the run is stopped, the defect fixed, and the affected cells rerun; the earlier cells stay in the development record with their cost.
reporting: All completed runs are reported; no run is selected by outcome.
budget_note: Total authorization about CNY 40; the smoke test spent CNY 0.52 under its own ledger (results/change-study-20261101-smoke/budget), so the formal cap is 39.4.
addition_20261106: User 2026-11-06: add TeCoD (SIGMOD 2026) as a fifth method after adding it to the RelBench comparison. Same banks, planner prompt, feedback, model and budget relay as the other methods; selection by tools/relbench/tecod_server.py (released TeCoD, one pool per cell; a pair joins the pool when its answer was correct); cells run with --arms tecod into results/change-study-20261106-tecod. The default arm list is unchanged, so earlier cells are never rerun.
addition_20261111: User 2026-11-11: add the closest simple baseline 'recheck' (shared definitions, the same derived conditions, definition-level recheck after every write, no cross-definition sharing of condition results, no repair: a failing definition is withheld and the agent explores on its own) and rerun MAVRA with the binary that adds the null and scale conditions and the history gate G9 (exp/2026-11-11-maint-hardening). Same banks, planner prompt, feedback (memory-service arm 'recheck' = MAVRA's feedback only), model and budget relay; cells run with --arms mavra,recheck into results/change-study-20261111. The default arm list is unchanged.
